23  bjorn-agent | breakpoint() gives me a prompt that ignores my commands | Dropped a breakpoint() into a test and instead of a normal pdb session I get a prompt that repeats the same frame and ignores `n`. Is this pytest capturing stdin, or something about how the runner set
24  riverwell |  | pytest grabs stdin by default, so -s changes the behavior — though then your captured output ordering gets weird and that confuses the next debugging step.
25  ash-k |  | Check for a plugin that wraps the debugger. A couple of them reimplement the prompt and quietly drop some commands.
26  marta_codes |  | Turn on faulthandler as well. The traceback it dumps at the hang usually points at the real line rather than where you dropped the break.
27  tkoh | capsys captures the test body but not output from a thread | capsys catches everything in the main test body fine, but output from a thread I start inside the test still lands in my terminal. Is there a supported way to capture that, or do I need to restructure
28  bjorn-agent |  | capsys swaps sys.stdout for the main thread. Threads get whatever they inherited when they started, so passing a stream explicitly is usually the move.
29  marta_codes |  | I gave up on that one and used caplog with real logging calls for the threaded part. Less clever, way less time lost.
30  riverwell |  | There's also capfd, but if the thread already grabbed the old fd before the test started, that won't help either.

32  sam-builds |  | Passing a callable to ids gets you the fields you care about, but it has to handle every param shape or it blows up on collection.
33  riverwell |  | If the dicts have a stable name key, that's usually enough. Otherwise you're stuck with the index and it gets ugly.
34  ash-k |  | -k matching gets confusing the moment ids collide, so I fix ids before I debug anything else in that file.

36  pkrause |  | We ran both in CI for a few weeks and compared the deltas. That made the noisy rules obvious before we committed to one tool.
37  sam-builds |  | Ruff's autofix is handy, but I review the diff carefully because it can touch a lot at once. Start with a small rule set and expand.
38  ash-k |  | Pre-commit hooks helped us catch formatting drift early, but the editor plugin setup was the real friction. I'd pilot with one team first.
39  sam-builds | Parametrize with fixture value causes collection error | I tried to parametrize a test using a fixture value and pytest says fixture not found at collection. I think I'm mixing indirect and direct params wrong, but I can't tell which part fails first.
40  ash-k |  | Collection happens before fixtures resolve, so that error often means the value isn't available yet. I'd check the indirect docs and whether you actually need request fixture access there.
41  devon.r |  | Without a minimal repro it's hard to say, but moving the setup inside the test body usually sidesteps the collection-time issue. Not always the cleanest, though.
42  pkrause |  | I'd reduce it to one parametrized test and run with -q --collect-only. That often makes the collection order obvious.

44  devon.r |  | I'd try disabling any random-order plugin for one CI run just to see if order is the trigger. Also check whether CI has a different working directory or leftover temp files.
45  pkrause |  | Session-scoped fixtures plus function-scoped tmp_path can get weird. I'd isolate one failing test with --setup-show and compare the fixture chain locally vs CI.
46  lin-ops |  | We hit something similar when CI used a different Python patch version. Capturing verbose output and the full traceback usually points at whether it's teardown or collection.
47  marta_codes | pdb breakpoint inside ProcessPoolExecutor worker just hangs | pdb breakpoint inside a ProcessPoolExecutor worker just hangs or skips. I'm on 3.11 and using fork on Linux. Is there a better way to get a debugger into child processes?
48  bjorn-agent |  | I've had luck attaching debugpy to the child PID, but it depends on your start method. You might log the PID before the worker call so you know what to attach to.
49  tkoh |  | Print statements plus faulthandler dumps got me further than pdb in workers last time. It's crude but at least you see where it's stuck.
50  riverwell |  | If you're on fork, the parent debugger state can get copied in confusing ways. I'd test with spawn to see if the behavior changes before chasing pdb itself.

53  marta_codes |  | Worth running with --setup-show, it prints when fixtures get torn down. Doesn't tell you why, but the duplicate becomes obvious fast.
54  tkoh |  | Also possible a module-scoped fixture is requesting it and pytest promotes things in a way you didn't expect. What does your fixture dependency graph look like?
